messages.subject: Activity Density Plot Error
parts:
Hey Juergen,

I'm working through some code I wrote a while back and am getting an error message for the following code, which seemed to work several months ago.

# Fix Dates & Times
Tegu.Act$Date.Time <- mdy_hm(Tegu.Act$Date.Time)

### Tegu Activity Density ###
TD <- activityDensity(Tegu.Act,
                      species = "TuMe",
                      allSpecies = FALSE,
                      speciesCol = "SpeciesCode",
                      recordDateTimeCol = "Date.Time",
                      recordDateTimeFormat = "%Y-%m-%d%H:%M:%S",
                      plotR = TRUE,
                      writePNG = FALSE,
                      plotDirectory,
                      createDir = FALSE,
                      pngMaxPix = 1000,
                      add.rug = TRUE,)

Error: datetime column must be a factor or character: recordTable[, recordDateTimeCol]
In addition: Warning message:
In if (!class(inputColumn) %in% c("factor", "character")) stop (paste("datetime column must be a factor or character:", : the condition has length >1 and only the first element will be used

My Date.Time is in POSIXct format: "2016-04-07 14:37:00"

I haven't been able to figure it out on my own and have not seen any questions with this specific error.

Any information on this would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks - Zach

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Activity Density Plot Error
parts:
Hi Zach,
I think I made some changes to the code to ensure the date/time column is either a character or factor. Actually, character makes a lot more sense than factor.
I can't recall the reasoning behind it at the moment (probably time zone issues since the timeZone argument is separate, but POSIX contains the time zone information). I admit that's not an ideal solution.
But you should be able to run the code fine if you simply convert the date/time column to character with
as.character(Tegu.Act$Date.Time)
before running activityDensity.
If that doesn't solve it I'll have a closer look.
Best regards,
Jürgen
